subject: Cooking
title: Lebanese Mezze: The Art of Sharing
description: A short lesson to help you apply Lebanese Mezze: The Art of Sharing.

hook.text: A Lebanese meal can have 40 small dishes on the table before the main course even arrives.

buildup.text: Mezze — from the Persian 'mazze' meaning taste — is a collection of small dishes served as appetizers.

discovery.text: Hummus, tabbouleh, baba ganoush, and fattoush all began as mezze — humble starters, now global stars.

twist.text: In Lebanon, the mezze often IS the meal. The 'main course' is almost an afterthought.

climax.text: Mezze culture influenced Spanish tapas, Turkish meze, and the global small-plates movement.

punchline.text: The best meals aren't served. They're shared.

quiz.question: What does the word 'mezze' derive from?

details.summary: Lebanese mezze is a spread of small dishes — hummus, baba ganoush, tabbouleh, fattoush — served communally before the main course.
details.whyItMatters: Mezze culture demonstrates food's social function beyond nutrition. The communal format builds connection and generosity, and its influence on global small-plates dining makes it one of the most impactful food service concepts in history.
takeaways: Mezze can include 20 to 40 small dishes in a full formal spread
Communal sharing is central to Lebanese hospitality and identity
The small-plates restaurant concept worldwide traces roots to mezze

faq.question: What are the essential mezze dishes?
faq.answer: Hummus, baba ganoush, tabbouleh, fattoush salad, labneh, muhammara, kibbeh, and warm pita bread form the core. A generous spread adds stuffed grape leaves, shanklish cheese, fried halloumi, and falafel. Each dish balances flavor and texture, and the variety ensures every palate is satisfied.

faq.question: How has mezze influenced global dining?
faq.answer: The small-plates concept exploded globally in the 2000s, but its roots are in mezze and tapas traditions. Sharing multiple small dishes creates more social interaction and variety than individual plated meals.
